title: The Way Down
description:
Daeun brought it up carefully.
"Minjun... this weekend, could you come down to the countryside with me? My mom has a hospital appointment."

Two train tickets. They sat side by side at the window. Seoul slid backward; rice paddies filled the glass.

After staring out the window a long while, Daeun spoke.
"Minjun, honestly — I'm scared."
"I came up to Seoul to be able to take care of her someday... and lately I'm not sure that's even a thing that can happen."

For the first time, the reason she'd held on for five years came out of her mouth with weight.

choices.text: "Whatever happens, I'll be right beside you." (Take her hand)
choices.result_text:
Daeun looked down at the hand holding hers. And smiled, a little.
"...You say things like that so easily, Minjun."
"I'm not saying it easily." When {name} said that, Daeun leaned her head against the window instead of answering.
The train kept going down, toward her hometown.

choices.text: Say nothing, and look out the window with her.
choices.result_text:
{name} said nothing. Instead, he looked where she was looking.

Instead of answering 'scared' with 'it'll be fine,' he just sat beside that fear.
After a long while Daeun said, quietly, "...It's a little easier, you looking at it with me."
The train kept going down, toward her hometown.

title: Her Mother's Table
description:
After the appointment, they had dinner at Daeun's country home.

Her mother wasn't one for words. Instead she kept heaping more rice into {name}'s bowl. "Eat more. You can't get food like this up in Seoul."

Then, out of nowhere, her mother glanced at {name}'s hands.
"...Hands that have worked hard."

In the middle of the table sat a gyeran-mari, the rolled omelet — yellow, thick, the ends neatly folded.
{name} knew that shape. It was the very same rolled omelet Daeun used to bring to his goshiwon in a side-dish container.
Without a word, he understood where it had come from.

choices.text: "Thank you for the meal, Mother." Finish the bowl with care.
choices.result_text:
{name} finished the bowl without leaving a single grain. Her mother saw it, and smiled for the first time, a little.

The night bus back. Daeun slept leaning against the window.
In one pane, the receding lights of the countryside and the approaching lights of Seoul were held together.

There had been nights spent counting three billion won. Tonight, for the first time, was a night he didn't have to count.

choices.text: "...So the gyeran-mari you used to make — it was your mother's."
choices.result_text:
Daeun stopped her chopsticks. Her face went a little red.
"...I copied hers. I'm still not as good as her."
At those words, her mother looked at her daughter for a long moment.

The night bus back. Daeun slept leaning against the window.
In one pane, the receding lights of the countryside and the approaching lights of Seoul were held together.

There had been nights spent counting three billion won. Tonight, for the first time, was a night he didn't have to count.

description_if_known.father_passed:
After the appointment, they had dinner at Daeun's country home.

Her mother wasn't one for words. Instead she kept heaping more rice into {name}'s bowl.
Then she asked, "And your parents, Minjun — what do they do?"

{name} lost his answer for a moment. His father was gone now. Not knowing what to say, he just looked at his bowl.
Her mother must have read the silence; she didn't ask again, only glanced at {name}'s hands.
"...Hands that have worked hard."

In the middle of the table sat a gyeran-mari, the rolled omelet — the very same one Daeun used to bring to his goshiwon.
Without a word, he understood where it had come from.

title: Three Days of Silence
description:
Three days, and no word from Jiyeon.

She was never one to reach out first. Still, three days was long.

Eleven at night. A knock at the door — Jiyeon, standing outside it.
No makeup, eyes that hadn't slept in days.

"...Oppa." She searched for the words a moment.
"Turns out tonight, this was the only place I had to go."

The woman who always looked down from the height of her own world stood, for the first time, lowered — outside {name}'s narrow door.

choices.text: Ask nothing, and open the door.
choices.result_text:
{name} asked nothing and stepped aside.
Jiyeon took off her shoes and came in. She looked once around the narrow room, then just sat on the floor.

"...You're not even going to ask."
"Do I have to?" When {name} said that, Jiyeon let the tension out of her shoulders for the first time.

choices.text: "What happened?" Ask without hiding the worry.
choices.result_text:
"What happened?" When {name} asked, Jiyeon let out a small laugh.
"...Of course that's the first thing you'd ask."
She didn't answer. Instead she took off her shoes, came in, and sat on the narrow room's floor.
"I'll stay a bit. ...That okay?"
{name} nodded.

description_if_known.arc_y3_jiyeon_departure_seen:
Three days, and no word from Jiyeon. With her down in Busan, contact was always sparse to begin with.

Still, three days was long.

Eleven at night. A knock at the door — Jiyeon, standing outside it.
The face of someone who'd taken the last late-night KTX up from Busan. No makeup, eyes that hadn't slept in days.

"...Oppa." She searched for the words a moment.
"Turns out tonight, this was the only place I had to go."

She'd left the wide house in Busan, caught the last train up, and the place she ended up standing was outside {name}'s narrow door.
The woman who always looked down from the height of her own world stood, for the first time, lowered.

title: The Narrow Room
description:
She sat in the narrow room, designer coat tossed off to one side, knees drawn up.

{name} poured water into two cup ramyeon. There was nothing else to offer.

Jiyeon looked slowly around the room. A few books, a folded blanket, one window. By the standards of her world, a room with nothing in it.

"This room is like you, oppa," she said.
"It's narrow... but all of it is real. My house is wide, and there's barely anything real in it."

Steam rose off the cup ramyeon and fogged the window pale.

choices.text: Say nothing, and hold her.
choices.result_text:
Instead of words, {name} held her. Jiyeon was stiff at first, then pressed her forehead into his shoulder.

"...The ramyeon's going soft," she said, but for a long while neither of them moved.
That night, the narrow room was exactly two people wide.

choices.text: Say nothing, and finish cooking the ramyeon, and set it down.
choices.result_text:
Instead of answering, {name} set the ramyeon in front of her. "Eat it before it goes soft."
Jiyeon split the wooden chopsticks. One bite, and she snorted a laugh.
"...It's good. Why is this good."
A night sharing two cup ramyeon in a narrow room — for her, it was the first.

description_if_known.told_jiyeon_about_records:
She sat in the narrow room, designer coat tossed off to one side, knees drawn up.

{name} poured water into two cup ramyeon. There was nothing else to offer.

Jiyeon looked slowly around the room. She knows now — whose son the owner of this room is, that the name was on the list her own father had ruined.

"...It's funny." Jiyeon said, looking down at the cup ramyeon.
"I'm eating ramyeon in the room of a man my dad ruined."

A cruelly honest thing to say. She didn't look away from it.
"But this room is like you, oppa. Narrow, and all of it real. My house is wide, and barely anything in it is."

title: The First Night
description:
After the wedding, they were finally alone. Their first home together was new, with half the boxes still unpacked.

At the threshold, Daeun could not quite make herself step inside. She kept turning her new ring with one fingertip. The white dress was gone, yet tonight she somehow looked unfamiliar.

"I..." Her voice was small. She took a breath, then chose not to hide.
"This is my first time, so... don't laugh."

The tips of her ears flushed red, but she did not look away. That was Daeun: shy, and honest enough to say so. {name} did not rush to answer. After an entire day spent in front of other people, the two of them were finally alone for the first time.

choices.text: Dim the lights and make something warm to drink.
choices.result_text:
Instead of answering, {name} lowered the living-room lights. He found two mugs that were still half wrapped in paper and put water on to boil.

As the kettle filled the little home with sound, Daeun finally crossed the threshold. Their shoes stood side by side.

choices.text: Don't hide it. "Tonight feels strange to me too."
choices.result_text:
"Tonight feels strange to me too."

Daeun's eyes widened. A moment later, a small laugh escaped with the breath she had been holding. "You too, Minjun? You looked like you knew exactly what you were doing."

description_if_known.daeun_hometown_visited:
After the wedding, they were finally alone in their first home.

At the threshold, Daeun turned her new ring with one fingertip.
"This is my first time, so... don't laugh." Her ears were red, but she did not look away.

Faced with that honesty, {name} remembered the table in her mother's country home: her mother silently heaping more rice into his bowl, those hands rolling a thick gyeran-mari, and her daughter carrying that same taste back to a goshiwon in a side-dish container.

By morning, that smell might fill this home too. For now, after an entire day spent in front of other people, the two of them were finally alone for the first time.

title: Tea Going Cold
description:
They sat side by side on the floor with warm mugs in their hands. The sofa was still wrapped in plastic, and an upturned moving box served as a table.

"Today went by too fast," Daeun said, watching the rim of her mug. "There was always someone looking at us. Taking pictures, saying hello, asking us to smile."

"No one's looking now."
"That's why I'm more nervous."

This time she did not laugh it away. As the steam faded from the tea, they slowly worked back through the whole day together.

choices.text: Set down the last cup and stand before her again.
choices.result_text:
The silence of this little home felt larger than the empty wedding hall. Daeun set down her mug and stood too.

"Minjun." Her voice still trembled, but this time she did not swallow what came next. "Come slowly."

title: Strange Together
description:
"Even saying we're married doesn't sound like my life yet," {name} said. "I woke up without a ring. Now there are two keys to this place. It's all good. It just arrived at once."

Daeun listened, then looked down at the hand wearing her ring.

"Then we're exactly the same."
"How?"
"We wanted to get here. We just haven't lived anything after this part before."

She stepped fully inside. The door clicked shut, and the thin blade of hallway light disappeared.

choices.text: "If it's strange for both of us, I think we'll be all right."
choices.result_text:
Daeun repeated it softly. "Strange for both of us... and all right."

Some of the tension left the words. Her fingertips still trembled. She did not hide them. She waited to see how {name} would come closer.

title: Before the Lights Go Out
description:
When the tea, the laughter, and the story of the day had all run quiet, they stood facing each other in the middle of the little living room. Even the refrigerator motor and the paper smell of unopened boxes felt sharp.

Daeun stopped turning her ring. Her eyes asked first, and she did not look away while {name} understood the question.

"What do we... do now?"

There was no correct answer. They only knew that neither of them had to hurry, and neither of them was going anywhere.

choices.text: Take her hand. "We can take it slow. I'm... nervous too."
choices.result_text:
"I'm... nervous too." His voice did not sound like itself either. Daeun's eyes widened, then she burst out laughing. "...What? You're shaking more than I am, Minjun." Her laughter loosened the taut air like a pulled thread. Their joined hands relaxed. Their foreheads drew close. Daeun closed her eyes, and the room went quietly dark.

The next morning, {name} woke to a familiar smell and a soft sizzle from the kitchen. Daeun had risen first. Still in the same clothes as last night, she was rolling gyeran-mari. The hands that had trembled now held a pan and wooden spatula.

{name} watched her from behind for a long while. Their first morning as a married couple began without a grand declaration, only the smell of breakfast meant for two.

choices.text: Ease her nerves with a joke. "Then let's call it my first time too."
choices.result_text:
"Then let's say tonight is my first time too." Daeun let out a small laugh and swatted his arm. "...Where did you learn to say things like that?" That single line relaxed shoulders that had been stiff as stone. She stepped closer, laughter still on her face. As the last distance between them disappeared, the room went quietly dark.

The next morning, {name} woke to a familiar smell and a soft sizzle from the kitchen. Daeun had risen first and was rolling gyeran-mari, still in the same clothes as last night.

{name} held the edge of the duvet and watched her for a long while. Without turning, Daeun somehow knew he was awake. "Give me a minute. The first one came out crooked." It was exactly the kind of mistake a first married morning should have.

title: The First Night
description:
After the wedding, they were finally alone. Jiyeon had leased their Seoul home in her own name, using the money she had saved and earned closing deals under her own name in Busan. The lease carried one name; the entryway held two pairs of shoes.

Jiyeon, usually the first to speak, had nothing to say tonight. She stood at the window, looking down at the city. The level of wine in her glass had not moved.

Silence from someone so proud was not the same thing as pride. By now, {name} knew her well enough to tell the difference.

"...Why are you just standing there?" As {name} approached, her shoulders tightened ever so slightly. Her reflection in the glass was redder than usual. Without turning, Jiyeon waited for what he would say next.

choices.text: Don't press. Stand beside her and look out at the same city.
choices.result_text:
{name} stopped one step away and looked through the same window. Their reflections stood side by side in the glass, though neither turned to the other.

Jiyeon lowered the wineglass a little. She knew at once that the person beside her was not going to demand that she fill the silence.

choices.text: Take the wineglass and set it on the table.
choices.result_text:
{name} took the wineglass from her hand and set it on the table by the window.

"You didn't drink any of it."
"If I got drunk, I'd have an excuse," Jiyeon said, finally turning around. "I could say the wine made me nervous."

title: Two People in the Glass
description:
The city moved silently below the glass. Jiyeon watched {name}'s reflection without turning her head.

"All day, people looked at everything except me."
"What did they look at?"
"The hotel. The dress. My father's face. No one asked whether any of it was what I chose."

Her voice stayed level, but her breath broke slightly on the last sentence. Jiyeon looked directly at {name} in the glass.

"What did you see, oppa?"

choices.text: "The person standing in front of me now."
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon finally turned away from the window. The smirk she had prepared never came. Neither did the quick remark meant to cover it.

"...You know answers like that are cheating, right?" Her voice was lower than usual. She did not look away.

title: A Night Without Excuses
description:
The wineglass made an unnaturally clear sound against the table. Once her hands were empty, Jiyeon looked even less certain what to do with them.

"So you're nervous without an excuse."
"You knew without making me say it."
"I did."
"That's more annoying."

She said it without stepping back. The woman who always used words to set the distance had left that distance for {name} to cross.

choices.text: Stay where you are, without pretending you heard too much or too little.
choices.result_text:
When {name} did not laugh, Jiyeon was the first to release a short breath.

"...Just like you, oppa. Only quick when it matters." It sounded like a complaint, but there was no barb at the end.

title: The Night She Set Down Her Armor
description:
The city lights had not changed, but the distance between their reflections had. Jiyeon was no longer watching the wineglass or the window.

The words she normally selected and placed with perfect control came late tonight. In that brief gap, tension and expectation occupied the same face.

"...Why are you looking at me like that?"

The sentence tried to sound proud and did not quite make it. {name} could leave the crack untouched, or give her something to push against.

choices.text: Respect her silence and offer a hand.
choices.result_text:
{name} asked nothing more. He simply held out his hand. Jiyeon looked down at it. One beat, then two. The Jiyeon he knew would have fired off a remark by now. Tonight, she took his hand without a word. Her fingers trembled faintly, and not from the wine. When {name} gently drew her closer, she came without resisting. The city lights blurred over them, and the room went quietly dark.

The next morning, {name} woke beside a face he had never seen before. Her makeup was gone. Her eyes were slightly puffy. None of the armor she normally kept perfectly in place remained. Jiyeon felt his gaze and pulled the duvet up to her nose.

"...What are you looking at? I always look like this in the morning." Her voice was curt, but the tips of her ears above the duvet were red. {name} had to work not to smile.

choices.text: Tease her gently. "Han Jiyeon, lost for words. That's a first."
choices.result_text:
"Han Jiyeon, lost for words. That's a first." Jiyeon spun around. "...Shut up." The words came sharp, but the tension in her face eased. Maybe being caught nervous was a relief. She stepped closer. "...Laugh and you're dead." The words were steady; her voice was not. The room went quietly dark.

The next morning, {name} woke beside a face he had never seen before. Her makeup was gone. Her eyes were slightly puffy. None of the armor she normally kept perfectly in place remained. Jiyeon felt his gaze and pulled the duvet up to her nose.

"...What are you looking at? I always look like this in the morning." Her voice was curt, but the tips of her ears above the duvet were red. A moment later, a low voice came from under the covers. "You're making the coffee, oppa."
